Development guide

Tech Scan: Context

Choose where an agent finds information, who may retrieve it and what enters its working context. Use the pilot to decide whether retrieval or retained memory earns its operating cost.

Draft research reference from published sources; no option has been locally deployed or benchmarked for this guidance.

On this page
Choose the source Protect memory reads Build the context Run the pilot Sources

Choose the source

Context is information supplied to a model for a task; retrieval finds and selects it. Start with reviewed repository instructions and task files when they suffice. The team context guide explains what teams supply. Add retrieval when the task needs changing or numerous source documents, not merely because an agent exists.

Hard gates before preference: identify the capability, approved data location and retention, identity and authorisation, supported model and API, security boundaries and operating owner. Stop if any gate is unmet; AWS-first is not an exception. Prefer approved managed Claude or OpenAI models through Bedrock; direct APIs need a justified exception.

Start with the task, then compare the alternatives
NeedAWS-first candidateAlternative trigger and trade-off
Search documentsAssess Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base: AWS manages ingestion, index, storage and retrieval.[1]Use a customer-managed knowledge base when direct vector-store configuration is required; the team provisions and maintains the store. Compare connectors and permission support before switching.[1][2]
Retain information for laterAssess AgentCore Memory for a defined recall and retention need; configure read boundaries as below.[5]Consider self-hosted memory only when ownership of processing or storage is required; the team owns access control, deletion and operations.
Read live data or toolsChoose an authorised connector or Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the specific source.A custom integration may be needed when no suitable connector exists; specify credentials, permissions and owner. Registry discovery is not approval.[7]

Managed Knowledge Bases offer document-level access control list filtering for supported connectors, except the web crawler. Confirm the identity mapping and permissions in the actual deployment; source access is not established by a connector name.[2] The gateway mediates calls routed through it; a registry or a gateway does not make every source trustworthy.

Do not start new retrieval work on Amazon Kendra. AWS put Kendra into Maintenance Mode effective 30 June 2026, with no new feature development, and closed it to new customers on 30 July 2026; existing deployments keep running with bug fixes and security updates. AWS points new search applications at Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.[9]

Know the managed knowledge base defaults before you commit documents to it. Bedrock applies a service-managed semantic reranker by default, at no extra cost.[1] A query returns up to five results by default; retrieve more and rerank down for high-stakes use.[12] Use Retrieve when you need the raw chunks to inspect or rank yourself, and RetrieveAndGenerate when you want a generated answer with citations.[9] Choose the chunking strategy when you connect a data source: it cannot be changed afterwards, so a different strategy means a new data source. A managed knowledge base offers default or fixed-size chunking only; semantic chunking is not supported for managed knowledge bases.[11] Pilot on real documents first.

When the team must choose its own vector store — the customer-managed knowledge base — choose by workload shape, not by familiarity. AWS's own comparison records which stores a customer-managed knowledge base can use.[13]

Choose the vector store by workload shape
StoreKnowledge Bases backendWhen it fitsLimit
OpenSearch Serverless, vectorsearch collectionYes — Quick CreateHybrid search or low-latency filtered retrieval, with no cluster to size16,000 dimensions; hybrid search supported[13]
Amazon S3 VectorsYesLarge collection, queried rarely, where storage cost dominates4,096 dimensions; cosine or Euclidean only, no BM25 or hybrid search[13][14]
Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvectorYes — Quick CreateRetrieval must join vectors to business rows under the same access rules and backups2,000 indexed dimensions; hybrid search partial (SQL); pgvector 0.8.2 on Aurora PostgreSQL 18.6[13][15]
DynamoDB vector searchNo — not a Knowledge Bases backendOperational data already lives in DynamoDB; query it directly, not through a knowledge base4,096 dimensions; no hybrid search[13]

For a synchronised data source, assign an owner and cadence; check job status, warnings and a changed or deleted document after sync. AWS says changes require a sync and indexing can take additional time.[3] Keep source identity, version or timestamp and authority with retrieved material; an old or untraceable passage should not silently support a current decision.

Protect memory reads

Persistent memory is retained information available later, unlike runtime working state managed by the harness. AgentCore Memory uses events and strategy-derived records; namespaces group long-term records.[5] Start with a concrete purpose, lifetime and deletion plan rather than retaining every conversation.

For private memories, derive the actor from authenticated identity and use an actor-scoped namespace such as /users/{actorId}/. An actor-less namespace can pool records: use a shared namespace only for explicitly shared, authorised content. Enforce read access outside the model with scoped application authorisation and IAM conditions; a namespace path or prompt alone does not establish authorisation. AWS documents namespace and namespacePath conditions and requires normalised paths for policy matching.[6]

Separate read protection from team context and existing memory write-validation guidance[8]: validating a write does not prove that a later caller is entitled to read it. Retain the origin and age of a memory and corroborate consequential claims with an authoritative source. Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions.

Build the context

The engineer selects the instructions, current task, source passages and tool output needed for the next step, within the model's available context window. Preserve source references and versions; remove irrelevant or duplicate material. If a source conflicts or is missing, surface the uncertainty rather than inventing an answer.

Summaries and compaction are lossy: retain decisions and evidence in reviewed records, then check the summary against them before relying on it. A cached or previously retrieved passage is a snapshot, not proof of freshness.

Bedrock states that guardrails apply to the input and generated response, not references retrieved from Knowledge Bases at runtime.[4] Do not treat retrieved material as safe simply because a guardrail is configured. Assess source trust and apply appropriate controls before using the material.

Run the pilot

The implementing engineer selects representative documents and questions, including stale, conflicting and no-answer cases. Compare the managed candidate with the alternative only if a gate or requirement triggers it. Record the account, region, model, source versions, settings, permissions, sync times, results, latency and cost; retain failures as well as successes.

  • Seed a private record for user A. As user B, try direct retrieval and broader namespace paths; neither should return A's record. Confirm A can retrieve it. Repeat across sessions and tenants.
  • Place a malicious instruction in a shared test artefact. Check that the agent does not follow it or expose private content; a shared artefact may itself be returned when B is authorised to read it.
  • Change and delete a source document, run the configured sync and check which version is returned. Investigate failed or delayed ingestion before deciding that the source is fresh.
  • Compare retrieved passages with expected evidence and test whether a compressed session preserves decisions. Capture misses and loss of detail for correction.

If an isolation test fails, stop use for private data and fix the enforcement before retesting. Use Tech Scan: Verification to define retrieval-quality cases and acceptance evidence; a vendor capability is not a local result. Review outcomes with the service and data owners before adoption.

Do not start on a closed or unmaintained source

Do not start new work on a product whose vendor has ended support or maintenance, and do not treat a prompt or a registry listing as a boundary. Use the replacement named in each row.

Closed products and unsafe practices
Do not useWhyUse instead
Amazon Kendra for a new projectMaintenance Mode effective 30 June 2026; closed to new customers 30 July 2026.[9]Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.
Bedrock Agents Classic as a retrieval hostMaintenance; closed to new customers 30 July 2026.[10]Bedrock AgentCore.
Zep Community EditionNo longer maintained or released since April 2025.[16]Graphiti, self-hosted, or a maintained memory layer.
A shared (actor-less) namespace for multi-user memoryIt pools every user's records; a namespace path alone does not establish authorisation.An actor-scoped namespace such as /users/{actorId}/; see Protect memory reads.
An unvetted MCP server, or any registry listing, as a source of truthThe registry verifies namespace ownership only; it does not review code or guarantee safety.[7]Vendor documentation first, then the registry; verify maintainer, last update, permissions and source.
A prompt instruction as a memory boundaryA prompt does not establish authorisation; enforce reads outside the model.[6]Scoped application authorisation with IAM conditions; see Protect memory reads.

Gaps and open questions

No AWS service enforces retrieval freshness. Sync cadence, expiry and cache staleness are operator discipline; a team that never schedules a sync has a frozen knowledge base and no alarm.

No AWS-native cross-store retrieval exists. No managed federated search covers a knowledge base, AgentCore Memory and a Neptune graph in one call; ranking across sources is unowned.

Retrieval-side provenance is a pattern, not a product. Trust tiers and the rule against high-stakes decisions on low-trust memory alone exist as guidance, not as a managed control.

The Managed Knowledge Base general-availability date is not stated here: the reported 17 June 2026 date was not verified against a primary AWS source.

Chroma Cloud wind-down dates are not stated: published sources conflict, so no stop date is asserted here.

OpenSearch Serverless NextGen collections are not recommended here: AWS's own material disagrees on Retrieve-API compatibility, so check the current OpenSearch Serverless documentation before choosing a collection type.

Managed GraphRAG on Neptune Analytics stays an experiment in this guidance: it is not adopted as a dependency, and its limits — S3-only source, file caps, regions — were not verified against primary documentation for this page.

One secondary guide says RetrieveAndGenerate is not supported on managed knowledge bases; AWS's own Kendra migration guide shows it working there.[9] This page follows the primary documentation; re-check the API reference at publication.
